title: Braun RT 20 table radio, 1963
lede: Dieter Rams’s table radio for Braun: a white steel face, tilted slightly back, with a circle of slots for the speaker and a column of grey knobs.
summary: White powder-coated face with a circular slot grille, grey knobs in a column, and a red tuning line. Rams for Braun, 1963.

creator.name: Dieter Rams, designer; Braun AG, manufacturer

evidence.note: Inspected the V&A’s primary image 2007BR3160 of object W.13-2007 at 1600 × 1067 px, through the V&A IIIF service.

styles.note: A clear case of the Braun grammar: a white face, perforation as the only texture, small lowercase labels, and one red signal on the scale.

context: The V&A describes an “oblong beechwood box with a white powder-coated sheet steel fascia tilted slightly backwards”, pierced with slots that form a circular loudspeaker, and says the speaker is concealed “with only pierced lines to indicate its presence”. [V&A W.13-2007](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O152458/).
The record transcribes the control labels in lowercase German: “höhen, tiefen, volumen, ein aus, phono, lang, mittel, ukw, sender”. [V&A](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O152458/).
observed: The front is one flat white panel inside a pale wood box. Its edge folds over the top with a small radius.
On the left, horizontal black slots of different lengths form a circle, split by a narrow vertical gap.
Three grey cylindrical knobs stand in a column in the centre, with a tiny label above each. Five small grey push buttons and one larger knob form a row along the bottom.
A tall, narrow tuning scale on the right carries fine black numerals and one red horizontal line, the only color on the face.
A small black “braun” logo sits above the knob column.
interpretation: The RT 20 shows the style’s one-signal rule: grey and white everywhere, and red only where the user reads the station.
borrow: Draw a circle from parallel lines of different lengths instead of a filled shape.
Give one thin line the only accent color, where the user reads a value.
